entry.name: dsp
entry.description: This is where you send the messages

attributes.name: annotation
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: attr_cpu
attributes.digest: Displays a rough estimate of how much of your computer's CPU is being allocated for processing audio in MSP.
attributes.description: Displays a rough estimate of how much of your computer's CPU is being allocated for processing audio in MSP.

attributes.name: attr_cpulimit
attributes.digest: Sets a limit (expressed in terms of a percentage of your computer's CPU)
attributes.description: Sets a limit (expressed in terms of a percentage of your computer's CPU) to how much signal processing MSP is allowed to do. MSP will not go above the set CPU limit for a sustained period, allowing your computer to perform other tasks without MSP locking them out. The trade-off, however, is that you'll hear clicks in the audio output when the CPU goes over the specified limit. Setting this value to either ‘0’ or ‘100’ will disable CPU limiting.

attributes.name: attr_drivername
attributes.digest: This pop-up menu lets you view and select the audio driver for MSP.
attributes.description: This pop-up menu lets you view and select the audio driver for MSP. Only one audio driver can be selected at any given time. MSP saves the settings for each audio driver separately and will recall the last used audio driver when you restart Max.

attributes.name: attr_dspstate
attributes.digest: Toggles turning the DSP on or off.
attributes.description: Toggles turning the DSP on or off

attributes.name: attr_funcalls
attributes.digest: Displays an approximate count of how many calculations are being required for each sample of audio.
attributes.description: Displays an approximate count of how many calculations are being required for each sample of audio.

attributes.name: attr_inchan1
attributes.digest: The pop-up menu is used to map the first logical input channel of I/O in MSP (i.e. the first outlet of theobject)
attributes.description: The pop-up menu is used to map the first logical input channel of I/O in MSP (i.e. the first outlet of theobject) to physical channels used by your audio driver.

attributes.name: attr_inchan2
attributes.digest: The pop-up menu is used to map the second logical input channel of I/O in MSP (i.e. the second outlet of theobject)
attributes.description: The pop-up menu is used to map the second logical input channel of I/O in MSP (i.e. the second outlet of theobject) to physical channels used by your audio driver. The contents of the pop-up menu will vary according to the audio driver you are using.

attributes.name: attr_inputdevicename
attributes.digest: Driver

attributes.name: attr_iovs
attributes.digest: Sets the number of audio samples samples that are transferred from the audio interface at one time when MSP is doing its calculations.
attributes.description: Sets the number of audio samples samples that are transferred from the audio interface at one time when MSP is doing its calculations. This number is always set to a power of 2.

attributes.name: attr_numinputs
attributes.digest: This value displays the number of available input channels.
attributes.description: This value displays the number of available input channels.

attributes.name: attr_numoutputs
attributes.digest: This value displays the number of available input channels.
attributes.description: This value displays the number of available input channels.

attributes.name: attr_optimize
attributes.digest: Vector Optimization
attributes.description: (Macintosh only) Toggles whether to select vector optimization in MSP when computing audio on processors that support it. Vector optimization allows four samples to be processed within the space of a single instruction. However, not all audio signal processing algorithms can be optimized in this way (e.g., recursive filter algorithms). Leaving this option on when using MSP will enhance CPU utilization and performance, although the exact performance gain depends on the algorithm you are using and the number of MSP objects that implement it that have been vector optimized.

attributes.name: attr_outchan1
attributes.digest: The pop-up menu is used to map the first logical output channel of I/O in MSP (i.e. the first inlet of theobject)
attributes.description: The pop-up menu is used to map the first logical output channel of I/O in MSP (i.e. the first inlet of theobject) to physical channels used by your audio driver. The contents of the pop-up menu will vary according to the audio driver you are using.

attributes.name: attr_outchan2
attributes.digest: The pop-up menu is used to map the second logical output channel of I/O in MSP (i.e. the second inlet of theobject)
attributes.description: The pop-up menu is used to map the second logical output channel of I/O in MSP (i.e. the second inlet of theobject) to physical channels used by your audio driver. The contents of the pop-up menu will vary according to the audio driver you are using.

attributes.name: attr_outputdevicename
attributes.digest: Driver

attributes.name: attr_overdrive
attributes.digest: Toggles running Max in Overdrive.
attributes.description: Toggles running Max in Overdrive. Whenis enabled, Max gives priority to timing and MIDI processing over screen drawing and user interface tasks such as responding to mouse clicks. If you are primarily going to be using Max for MIDI or audio processing, Overdrive should be enabled. If you are primarily going to be using Jitter, Overdrive should be disabled.

attributes.name: attr_siai
attributes.digest: Toggles running the Max Scheduler in Audio Interrupt when Overdrive is enabled.
attributes.description: Toggles running the Max Scheduler in Audio Interrupt when Overdrive is enabled. This feature runs the Max event scheduler immediately before processing a signal vector’s worth of audio. Enabling Sched-uler in Audio Interrupt can greatly improve the timing of audio events that are triggered from control processes or external MIDI input.

attributes.name: attr_sigsused
attributes.digest: Displays the number of internal buffers that were needed by MSP to connect the signal objects used in the current signal network.
attributes.description: Displays the number of internal buffers that were needed by MSP to connect the signal objects used in the current signal network. This field will update update whenever you change the number of audio objects or how they are patched together.

attributes.name: attr_sr
attributes.digest: The pop-up menu is used to set the audio sampling rate.
attributes.description: The pop-up menu is used to set the audio sampling rate. For full-range audio, the recommended sampling rate is 44.1 kHz. Using a lower rate will reduce the number of samples that MSP has to calculate, thus lightening your computer’s burden, but it will also reduce the frequency range.

attributes.name: attr_vs
attributes.digest: Sets the number of audio samples samples that are transferred to the audio interface at one time when MSP is running.
attributes.description: Sets the number of audio samples samples that are transferred to the audio interface at one time when MSP is running. This number is always set to a power of 2, and can be less than or equal to the I/O Vector Size, but not more. If the Signal Vector Size is less than the I/O Vector Size, MSP calculates two or more signal vectors in succession for each I/O vector that needs to be calculated.

messages.name: advancedstatus
messages.digest: The wordopens the advanced Audio Status window.
messages.description: The wordopens the advanced Audio Status window.

messages.name: cpulimit
messages.digest: The word, followed by a number in the range 0-100, sets a utilization limit for the CPU. Above this limit, MSP will not process audio vectors until the utilization comes back down, causing a click. If the cpu limit is set to either 0 or 100, there will be no limit checking done.
messages.description: The word, followed by a number in the range 0-100, sets a utilization limit for the CPU. Above this limit, MSP will not process audio vectors until the utilization comes back down, causing a click. If the cpu limit is set to either 0 or 100, there will be no limit checking done.

messages.name: debug
messages.digest: The word, followed by a zero or one, turns debugging on (1) or off (0).
messages.description: The word, followed by a zero or one, turns debugging on (1) or off (0).

messages.name: driver
messages.digest: Themessage to dsp is a way to send messages specific to a particular audio driver.
messages.description: Themessage to dsp is a way to send messages specific to a particular audio driver. For documentation of any driver-specific messages, consult the documentation for the audio driver.

messages.name: driversetup
messages.digest: Opens the Audio Driver Setup window
messages.description: Opens the Audio Driver Setup window

messages.name: iovs
messages.digest: The word, followed by a number that is a power of 2, sets the I/O vector size.
messages.description: The word, followed by a number that is a power of 2, sets the I/O vector size.

messages.name: open
messages.digest: The wordopens the Audio Status window.
messages.description: The wordopens the Audio Status window.

messages.name: optimize
messages.description: (Macintosh only) Toggles optimization. On the Macintosh, this is used to control the use of Altivec (G4 processor) optimizations.

messages.name: override
messages.description: Toggles override mode. When override mode is enabled, any change to the setting is not saved in the MSP Preferences file. The messageturns override mode off. By default, override is off for all settings. However, some settings are specific to audio drivers and may not be saved by the driver.

messages.name: set
messages.digest: The word, followed by a zero or one, turns the audio on (1) or off (0). It is equivalent to clicking on aorobject.
messages.description: The word, followed by a zero or one, turns the audio on (1) or off (0). It is equivalent to clicking on aorobject.

messages.name: setdriver
messages.digest: The word, followed by a number, sets a new audio driver is chosen based on its index into the currently generated menu of drivers created by thedriver object. If the wordis followed by a symbol that names a valid driver, the new driver is selected by name. An additional symbol argument may be used to specify a "subdriver" (e.g., ASIO drivers use ASIO as the name of the driver and PCI-324 as a subdriver name that specifies a specific device).
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets a new audio driver is chosen based on its index into the currently generated menu of drivers created by thedriver object. If the wordis followed by a symbol that names a valid driver, the new driver is selected by name. An additional symbol argument may be used to specify a "subdriver" (e.g., ASIO drivers use ASIO as the name of the driver and PCI-324 as a subdriver name that specifies a specific device).

messages.name: sigvs
messages.digest: The word, followed by a number that is a power of 2, sets the I/O signal vector size.
messages.description: The word, followed by a number that is a power of 2, sets the I/O signal vector size.

messages.name: sr
messages.digest: The word, followed by a number, sets a new sampling rate In Hertz.
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets a new sampling rate In Hertz.

messages.name: status
messages.digest: The wordopens the Audio Status window.
messages.description: The wordopens the Audio Status window.

messages.name: takeover
messages.digest: The word, followed by a zero or one, turns Scheduler in Audio Interrupt mode on (1) or off (0). It is equivalent to clicking on the Scheduler in Overdrive checkbox in the Audio Status window.
messages.description: The word, followed by a zero or one, turns Scheduler in Audio Interrupt mode on (1) or off (0). It is equivalent to clicking on the Scheduler in Overdrive checkbox in the Audio Status window.

messages.name: timecode
messages.digest: The wordfollowed by a zero or one, starts (1) or stops (0) timecode reading by any audio drivers that support the feature (ASIO 2).
messages.description: The wordfollowed by a zero or one, starts (1) or stops (0) timecode reading by any audio drivers that support the feature (ASIO 2).
